checks: Verified original §§3–4, equations (3)–(6), with the source balance retained. The factor 4 in the Hessian comes from differentiating P_i^(-3)/(3 E_i) twice. Every present denominator is positive in a common open convex domain containing K.

On a constant-profile facet the continuous representative is convex and is an allowed facet test by the preceding hinge characterization. The squared-density integral forces that representative to vanish; nonnegative Hessian terms then each have zero tangent component.

Positive definite A excludes uncrossed facets. A proper line meets the boundary in exactly two points, neither can lie on more than one open facet, and supporting traces have zero arclength. This yields at most 2m facets even with coincident cut lines.

On complementary arcs, continuity upgrades the almost-everywhere level equality to pointwise equality. A critical point of the strictly convex G would be its unique strict minimum, so no point of a nontrivial level arc is critical. The tangential Hessian over gradient norm is strictly positive curvature. Continuity matches the constants across an isolated crossing and across the whole boundary when facetless.

In rank one every positive normal is in range A, and the exact balance puts each relevant projective parameter there. Strict scalar convexity gives at most two lines per level; at most two uncrossed facets have tangent ker A. An unexhausted complementary open arc would contain a segment on such a level line and hence already lie in a facet.
